Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@acmehealth.com>

Subject: Questions on DPA: residency / retention / deletion

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the proof-of-concept demo last week. Our legal team sent over a short set of DPA redlines and a few questions we can't resolve without vendor confirmation. Attached: Acme_DPA_redlines_v2.docx (highlights in yellow). High level questions:

- Residency: We need all customer data and audit logs to be stored and processed only within the EU for the Acme Health account. Is Redwood able to guarantee both primary and DR copies in-region, or do you rely on contractual safeguards for cross-border replication?
- Retention: We see a 90-day logs retention default in the DPA. Can that be shortened to 30 days for audit logs and 90 days for application data?
- Deletion: When a customer requests erasure, we require a signed certificate of deletion and an explicit backup purge window. What is Redwood's standard for (a) live data deletion, (b) backup purge, and (c) certificate issuance timeline?
- Subprocessors: Please confirm subprocessors used for backups and metrics for Acme Health specifically.

We'd like to get a short call on Monday (Nov 22) if possible to walk through and close any items.

Best,
Sara
Sara Kim
Lead Counsel, Privacy & Regulatory
Acme Health

Subject: Re: Questions on DPA: residency / retention / deletion

Hi Sara — thanks for sending these over and for the thorough notes. I've looped in our legal (Priyom) and privacy (Neha) teams to make sure we provide language you can put into a contract. Attached: Redwood_DPA_response_v1.docx — contains proposed redline language and brief rationale. High-level responses below so you have a summary before we dive into the doc: 

- Residency: We offer a region-selection option where production data and primary backups are pinned to an EU region (customer-managed residency). For DR and long-term backups, our standard is encrypted multi-region replication; however, we can commit to geo-restrictions for Acme Health under an addendum or by using our Private (VPC) offering. Proposed contract language in the doc that allows an "in-region-only" obligation for both primary and backups with subprocessors restricted to EU-based providers.

- Retention: Redwood's out-of-the-box defaults are 90 days for audit logs and configurable retention for customer data. We can accept a contractual change to 30 days for audit logs (as you requested) provided we include a short carve-out for forensic copies retained during active investigations or legal holds. Suggested clause in the redline.

- Deletion/certification: We can confirm live data deletion within 48 hours of an erasure request; backups are more complex — our typical secure-erase lifecycle for backups completes within 60 days, and we can provide a certificate of deletion within 10 business days after completion of the purge. For EU-only accounts we can tighten that to a 30-day backup purge window (with an exception for legal hold). Proposed wording in the doc.

- Subprocessors: I included a list of primary subprocessors and a commitment to notify you 30 days before adding new EU-located subprocessors that will process Acme data.

We'll plan to hold a 30-minute call Monday to run through the redline unless you'd prefer to continue via email. Proposed time: Nov 22, 10:00 CET.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this quickly.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
redwood.com

Subject: RE: Questions on DPA: residency / retention / deletion (internal legal notes)

Internal note (do not send yet):

I reviewed Acme's redlines and Laura's proposed responses. A few suggested edits before we send the redline back:

1) Residency pledge — we should avoid absolute language for DR unless Acme signs up for our Private (VPC) option or we include an explicit addendum covering on-prem synchronous replication. Alternative: "Redwood shall store and process Customer Content within the EU for production workloads and will not intentionally transfer Customer Content outside the EU except for temporary, encrypted backups necessary for disaster recovery; such transfers will be subject to the restrictions in Section X and Subprocessor Appendix."

2) Backup purge window — Acme asks for 30 days in backups; operationally we can accept 30 days for EU-only accounts provided they accept a 30-day hold exception for legal holds and forensic needs. Wording: "Backups containing Customer Content will be purged within thirty (30) days following deletion, except to the extent required by law or bona fide legal hold; Redwood will provide a signed certificate of deletion within ten (10) business days following completion of the purge."

3) Audit logs — agree to 30 days for audit logs but add a short exception: "Audit logs required for security incident investigations may be retained up to 180 days on an as-needed basis with Customer notification." Keep that scoped and require joint approval for extended retention.

4) Subprocessor transparency — commit to a 30-day notice + opportunity to object (reasonable grounds) for new EU subprocessors. For third-party backup providers, list current vendors and include a process for Acme to request onshore-only vendor use (may trigger additional charges).

If everyone is aligned, I'll incorporate into the redline doc and recommend we table any absolute-residency warranty for anything but production/primary backups unless they buy Private.

Priyom
Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference

Hi Sara — following up with updated language and a few concessions we can make for Acme Health (see inline redlines in the attached document). Summary of the key contractual edits we've proposed: 

- In-region guarantee (production + primary backups): We will commit to storing and processing Customer Content within the EU (specified region) for production and primary backups. Disaster recovery/backups used solely for long-term archival will be geographically restricted to EU data centers; any temporary cross-border replication for failover requires Customer consent. (Redline provided.)

- Backup purge timeline: For EU-only accounts we are offering a 30-day backup purge window after deletion request, with a legal-hold carve-out. Redwood will provide a signed certificate of deletion within 10 business days after the purge completes.

- Audit logs: We accept 30 days by default; security incident investigations can justify retention up to 180 days with Customer notification and a jointly documented justification.

- Subprocessors: We will add current EU subprocessors to Appendix A and notify Acme 30 days prior to onboarding any new subprocessors that will process Acme Content. If Acme requires use of a specific onshore-only backup vendor, we can accommodate under a commercial addendum.

If these changes look acceptable, let's confirm the Monday call for Nov 22, 10:00 CET to finalize. If you prefer a tracked-redline exchange, we're happy to proceed that way too.

Thanks — Laura
